newsitem.title: NORWAY: NATO ministers start planning new Bosnia force.
newsitem.headline: NATO ministers start planning new Bosnia force.

text.p: NATO defence ministers took a significant step on Wednesday towards keeping thousands of troops in Bosnia next year after the mandate of the current peace mission runs out in late December.

NATO diplomats said the 16 ministers, meeting informally in this Norwegian port city, accepted some sort of force would probably be necessary, but wanted the military to start work on a range of options.
"No-one spoke against keeping a force there," said one NATO official.

Diplomats said the ministers wanted NATO's military to begin work on an assessment of the tasks any "follow-on" force to the 52,000-strong Implementation Force (IFOR) would be required to do and a clear statement of the mission's aims.
They said NATO's policy-making North Atlantic Council would formally instruct the military to begin preparations at the next weekly meeting in Brussels.
Four options for the force, which is certain to involve U.S. grounds troops, would be considered:
-- total withdrawal of the existing force
-- a deterrence force limited to preventing an outbreak of fresh fighting
-- a deterrence force with a wider mandate to provide a general security framework
-- a force fulfilling deterrence and giving support to civilian reconstruction efforts.
